title: Testing an app created to support emotion regulation in young people with ADHD symptoms
official: Prototyping a digital health intervention to support emotion regulation in young people with ADHD symptoms
summary:
Background and study aims
Young people with ADHD symptoms often experience difficulties managing emotions, but there are no accessible interventions designed specifically to support these young people in developing emotion regulation skills. This study will evaluate a new smartphone app co-designed with young people with ADHD, their parents/caregivers, and clinicians. The study aims to examine whether using the app provides preliminary evidence of improvement in emotion regulation, anxiety and depression, and whether the app is acceptable and engaging for young people with ADHD symptoms.

Who can participate?
The study will include 50 young people aged 11–15 who have an ADHD diagnosis or are on an NHS waiting list for ADHD assessment. They must live in England or Scotland, be able to complete the study in English, and have access to a compatible smartphone or tablet. Parents/caregivers can also take part as optional informants.

What does the study involve?
Young people will complete a short screening questionnaire and, if eligible, a baseline questionnaire. They will then use the app for four weeks and complete a follow-up questionnaire. Parents/caregivers who choose to take part will also complete baseline and follow-up questionnaires about their young person. Some young people will also be invited to take part in an optional interview about their experience of using the app.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
There are no direct benefits from taking part. However, participants will contribute to improving future resources and support for young people with ADHD symptoms. Some questions or app content about emotions and mental health may cause temporary discomfort or distress, and participation may involve some time burden.

Where is the study run from?
University of Edinburgh (UK)

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
September 2026 to March 2027

Who is funding the study?
Medical Research Council (UK)

Who is the main contact?
Daria Melashenko, dmelashe@ed.ac.uk

interventions.name: A self-guided smartphone app called ER-ADHD was designed to support emotion regulation in young people with ADHD symptoms. The app delivers short, interactive modules teaching strategies for understanding and managing emotions and is used for 4 weeks.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Participants will be young people and one of their parents or caregivers.

Young person participants:
1. Age: Aged between 11 and 15 years at the time of consent/assent
2. Diagnosis: Have a clinical diagnosis of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) or be on  waiting list for diagnostic assessment for ADHD Language: Have sufficient English comprehension and literacy to read and understand the participant information, assent materials and app content
3. Access to technology: Have access to a compatible smartphone
4. Consent/assent: Have parental consent and be able to provide informed assent to take part in the study
5. Location: Reside in England or Scotland and be able to take part fully online

Parent/caregiver participants:
1. Must be the parent or primary caregiver (biological, adoptive, or legal guardian) of an eligible young person who has
provided assent to take part
2. Must have sufficient English proficiency to read and understand study information and questionnaires
3. Must provide informed consent to participate
4. Parent/caregiver participation is optional, but parents/caregivers will only be invited to complete these questionnaires if
their child meets the emotion dysregulation eligibility threshold
Exclusion criteria:
To maximise the representativeness of the sample, there will be no exclusion criteria based on co-occurring
neurodevelopmental or mental health issues.

Young person participants:
1. Mild-to-none range of emotion dysregulation: Young people whose scores on the eligibility questionnaire indicate mild-to-none emotion dysregulation will not be eligible to continue, as the intervention is designed to be most appropriate for those experiencing moderate to severe difficulties
2. Significant cognitive or language difficulties: Young people who would be unable to understand the study materials, app content or questionnaires due to cognitive impairment or limited English proficiency will be excluded to ensure informed and meaningful participation
3. Lack of consent/assent: Young people will not be eligible if their parent or caregiver does not provide consent, or if the young person does not provide informed assent
4. Lack of access to required technology: Young people without access to a smartphone will be excluded, as this would prevent them from using the app being tested

Parent/caregiver participants:
1. Do not have parental responsibility for the participating young person
2. Do not provide informed consent to participate
3. Have significant cognitive or language difficulties that would prevent them from understanding the study materials or
completing the optional questionnaires
4. Have insufficient English proficiency to understand the consent process or complete the optional questionnaires
